It's a pretty fun game.  The story lines, while so far pretty short and unconnected, are well written and enjoyable.  As a software engineer who spends a lot of time in a terminal, the game's approximation of a terminal is pretty good, albeit limited in functionality (grep, maybe? :)).  If you're not familiar with common linux commands, the game will teach you commands that you can really use (scp and a few others are more complex than in the game).  The strategies for hacking a system are also pretty legit, the game is a great way to get a high-level understanding of what hackers exploit.  That said, because it's a game (and not the Anarchist's Cookbook), how to write a script that cracks a given port is obfuscated from the player.  You simply download an existing .exe and you execute it... no actual scripting.  That's not at all to the game's detriment, as it's very enjoyable to have to fuss with all the minutia when the trace timer is counting down. 

It'd be nice to see an update, or a DLC, that contains a more congruent story line, not lots of short and disconnected stories.  Maybe a few (more) terminal easter eggs, I have yet to find one.  And definitely some harmless and optional scripting (obviously don't teach us to really hack a port). :) 

I'd say this game is a 7 - 7.5/10.  Definitely worth the purchase.

The best Hollywood hacking game ever! Alright, so there are like three of those ever, but this is still all kinds of great. The missions here each feel like there's a touch of character, a reason behind them that just passes the threshold of generic gamestory and hits that spot of "I am a hacker at my computer." (Even if you're just ultimate script kiddie.)

Hacknet is an ever evolving experience, constantly throwing you through unexpected hoops and challenges that all manage to make perfect sense in its world while still being completely inside all the mechanics of the game. The best of these are all spoilers and are best when they take you by surprise. The moments of, "I didn't think that could happen!" Followed by, "Of course, that makes perfect sense," then, "but how do I fix this?" All within all the rules you've seen thus far. It's like you're always in control, always the hacker, actually working to hack the hackables.

Oh, and the music is spectacualr. A combination of tailor made electronic-technomancer and artists like Carpenter Brut provide the background to Hacknet and I've never seen better use of mixing. It understands when songs should be quiet, when they should hit you, when to be solem and when to kick you into high gear. Coupled with an incredible UI that proves itself time and time again to make more sense than you thought leaves you more immersed than you can be with real hacking.

[h1] Overview	[/h1]
I thought the game was good. It had a decent story, but there were some aspects there were missing. 

For example: This was one of the first hacking genre games I played, so walking into this game I was waiting for the complications to arise. Oh boy. Did they ever.

See, when I am introduced into a new game, I expect a tutorial. This game gave me an under cooked version of that. When I loaded up the game, it game me a protocol and I needed to execute that, but it game me no idea of what to do. What commands anything. So, I looked and I looked, and hidden on the right side there was a tutorial. It was helpful but it didn't help me remember later in the game, So I had to keep referring to the tutorial.

[h1] Overall...	[/h1]
It was a thrilling game. It got my heart beating here and there like I was on a roller-coaster or I was watching a horror movie. So, I give my condolences on that part. The music was golden. I really loved the electronic style that was incorporated in the UI. The animations and the art were also amazing. I loved the probe art and movements that were made. The story was a little raw, but I need to play more of these hacking genre games to made a more logical inference.

And Yes. I recommend this game. Even though I am not that knowledgeable with hacking I do recommend this game to new comers that have a sense of patience. I had a rough time with that, but I hope who ever looks at this keeps that in mind, because I went through a lot of digging to figure out what the hell to do to pass the tutorial. 

[h1] Edit: [/h1]
Looking back at this and continuing playing the game later on in my life, it is a game that you can't play a little of and then come back to it. There is a lot that you have to remember and trying to come back after a while and continue, it leaves me confused and looking online for all of the commands only to find out later that there was a command for that too.

While it is a fun game, there is a lot of knowledge that is required to successfully complete this game with flying colors. You need to be quick and you need to be able to keep a solid list of things that you do when going about managing your tracks and how it impacts the game later.
